title: Dashboard canvas - interactive debugging and TTL guidelines
body:
Context:
This doc proposes a lightweight "dashboard canvas" pattern for interactive debugging of inference incidents and a set of panel TTL/query-throttling guidelines to control dashboard query cost. It is meant as an ops-friendly layer between our raw metric stores and the large investigative dashboards we hand to SREs and product engineers.

Goals:
- Make fast investigation reproducible: one-click drill links from a dashboard card into a trace slice or prompt-replay view.
- Keep dashboard query cost predictable: enforce TTLs and throttles per widget, plus inexpensive summary panels for on-call.
- Reduce cognitive load: compact micro-SLIs + contextual annotations rather than giant multi-pane dashboards.
- Provide clear instrumentation hints so product/infra owners know what to add/trim.

Design patterns (high level):
1) Card + Trace Primer: each interactive card shows a 1-line SLI, 3 small trend sparklines, then 2 action links: "open trace slice" and "replay prompt". The trace link passes a compact filter (tenant, route, request-id prefix) so the trace UI fetches at most ~200 spans.

2) TTL tiers for panels:
- fast-panels (15s refresh): short-term troubleshooting for oncall (only top-10 tenants/cohorts, heavy downsampling).
- steady-panels (1m refresh): product dashboards for daily work.
- long-panels (5m refresh): executive/SE dashboards, aggregated, decimated.
Rules: default to "steady" unless marked fast. Panels that run expensive joins (router->kv-cache->model) must be long-panel or use precomputed rollups.

3) Query throttling and user gating:
- UI enforces per-user/role concurrency limits for heavy panels (e.g., max 2 concurrent runs of the full per-tenant heatmap).
- Client-side UI shows a token bucket meter for heavy queries; operators can borrow 1-minute grace tokens for incidents.

Investigation UX (concrete flow):
- Symptom observed (alert) -> click fast-card -> filter auto-populated: time window = last 5m, tenant = alert tenant, route = route-tag.
- Card expands to show top 5 correlated traces (scored by latency * error count), then an inline sample of the top trace spans + first 3 tokens of prompt.
- If operator clicks "open trace" -> trace UI opens with the pre-applied filter + sampling override to capture full trace (one-shot). This requires a short-lived sampling bump token issued by the dashboard backend (ops-only).

Instrumentation checklist for owners (short):
- Ensure request_id propagation across API -> router -> runtime -> model-host.
- Annotate spans with: tenant_id, route, model_variant, kv_cache_hit (bool), batch_size (int), prompt_truncated (bool).
- Emit short event with 'prompt-hash' to link metric slices to prompt-replay store. Hash must be reversible only inside platform (store raw prompt separate w/ access controls).

PromQL / SQL snippets (examples):
- Cheap per-route 95p latency, sampled:
  rate(runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket{job="runtime",le="1.0"}[5m])
  / ignoring(le) group_left sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_seconds_count{job="runtime"}[5m]))
  // note: use histogram_quantile client-side for nicer deciles

- KV cache heatmap (pre-aggregated):
  SELECT tenant, route, kv_bucket, count FROM obs_kv_heatmap_rollup WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 hour' LIMIT 500
  // prefer rollups; avoid full scan queries in fast panels

Prioritization matrix for trimming panels (one-line rules):
- If panel queries more than 3 tables and runs more often than 1m => candidate for rollup
- If panel returns >1000 series and is used < 2x/day => archive to a weekly summary
- If panel correlates to a low-severity SLI change and costs > $X/day => require owner sign-off to keep it as fast panel

Open questions / risks (short list):
- Trace sampling override risk: how to ensure we don't explode trace storage during incident storms? Proposal: one-shot override tokens limited to 100 traces per incident and auto-evict. Need SRE guardrails and budget alerting.
- Prompt replay PII: stored prompts could contain sensitive customer input. We need encryption at rest and per-customer retention controls.
- Role model: who can create "fast" panels? Suggest restrict to SRE + product leads; others request via ticket.

Operational runbook snippets (to be included in oncall quickcards):
- If you see spike in tail latency: click the "tail-latency smallcard" -> verify top tenant -> open trace -> check kv_cache_hit false or high batch_size. If kv misses, escalate to runtime-team.
- If you need more traces: request a sampling-bump token from ops-telemetry channel with incident id (automated via bot). Token auto-expires.

Action items (next 90d):
- [ ] Implement TTL tiers in dashboard UI (Marco)
- [ ] Add trace-link payload schema and one-shot sampling tokens (Evan)
- [ ] Audit existing fast-panels and tag candidates for rollup (Tanya + product owners)
- [ ] Draft retention + encryption policy for prompt-replay store (security + legal)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Could embed a tiny decision tree on each card: "Is latency spike tenant-wide? -> Yes: show top tenants; No: show trace snippets".
- We should standardize a small set of "card actions" (open-trace, open-replay, throttle-panel, snapshot-to-s3) so ownership and instrumentation are consistent.

References and links:
- Linear ticket for UX: OBS-412 (linked above)
- Repo with rollup schema: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-rollups (PR linked above)
- Slack thread: #observability-ops (linked above)

If you're reading: please add quick comments below with use-cases where you rely on heavy dashboard panels and we can prioritize which to keep as fast.
